# Neil Artus - Backend & AI Software Engineer

> I build distributed backend systems, applied AI, and cloud infrastructure. My work spans enterprise automation at Emerson and JG Summit, streaming research agents, and embedded AI prototypes. I focus on the systems behind the interface: APIs, data pipelines, authentication, and deployment.

Last updated: 2026-09-05. Biography and private-project descriptions are owner-provided. Public repository links document implementation details, not independently audited outcomes.

## Projects

### AGOS: Agentic Philippine Market Intelligence Platform

Philippine market research platform with a React interface, FastAPI services, and ingestion pipelines for market, economic, and news data.

Concurrent research, portfolio, and risk workers stream responses through Server-Sent Events. The backend uses DeepSeek, while Gemini supports news ingestion. Cosmos DB stores research data; Firebase verification and rate limiting support API access control.

- Focus: Market research infrastructure
- Stack: FastAPI, Python, DeepSeek, SSE, Cosmos DB, Firebase, SlowAPI, React
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#agos)
- [Live site](https://agos-agentic.vercel.app)
- [Source code](https://github.com/NeilR2s/agos)
- [Technical documentation, inspected revision](https://github.com/NeilR2s/agos/blob/6712e42b3f34a3edae460aaedd52221ca61bc83e/README.md)

### Enterprise HR Automation Engine

Python-based attendance reporting workflow with authenticated access to employee records.

Combines report automation, Linux-hosted backend services, and Microsoft Entra ID role-based access. Source code and internal implementation records are not publicly available.

- Focus: Reporting workflows
- Stack: Python, Hetzner, Nginx, Entra ID
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#hr-automation)
- Source not published

### MediSeen: Clinical Decision Support Platform

Clinical decision-support research prototype with a web interface and streamed AI responses.

Connects an AI-assisted interface to cloud-hosted backend services. This is a research prototype, not a substitute for professional medical assessment; source code is not publicly available.

- Focus: Applied AI prototype
- Stack: FastAPI, React, Azure, Cloudflare, Tailwind CSS, SSE
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#mediseen)
- [Live site](https://mediseen-2.vercel.app)
- Source not published

### CNN-Osteo: Thermal-Image Screening Prototype

Research prototype using TensorFlow and MobileNetV3Small to classify thermal knee images into osteoarthritis-related categories, with Raspberry Pi as the deployment target.

The model card credits Neil with model training and inference, Joshua Lawrence C. Contreras with the UI, and Contreras, Hadji Luis L. Montealegre, and Francis G. Yaeso as the thesis researchers. Intended as a screening aid, not a standalone diagnostic tool; the model card documents limitations in generalizability.

- Focus: Embedded AI research
- Stack: Python, TensorFlow, MobileNet, Raspberry Pi, NumPy
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#cnn-osteo)
- [Source code](https://github.com/NeilR2s/raspberry-pi-osteoarthritis-detection)
- [Technical documentation, inspected revision](https://github.com/NeilR2s/raspberry-pi-osteoarthritis-detection/blob/60b145406b2995f1582db8183e3198a0053a9d7f/README.md)

### AlerSense: Attention-Monitoring Prototype

Demonstration prototype combining ESP32 telemetry, a Python video-inference component, a Flask-SocketIO API, and a Next.js dashboard.

FreeRTOS queues separate sensor work from network transmission, with a drop-on-full policy. The API broadcasts telemetry to the dashboard.

- Focus: IoT telemetry prototype
- Stack: C++, ESP32, FreeRTOS, Flask-SocketIO, Next.js
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#alersense)
- [Live site](https://alersense.vercel.app)
- [Source code](https://github.com/NeilR2s/alersense)
- [Technical documentation, inspected revision](https://github.com/NeilR2s/alersense/blob/9d94de561cac44c641d116819e108cb41acb0dd4/README.md)

### DFA Visualizer: Formal Language Workbench

Browser-based React and TypeScript workbench for DFA simulation (automata and formal languages), right-linear grammar derivation, and derived PDA simulation.

Runs automata locally in TypeScript, with SVG visualizations and parity-check tooling against a Python reference implementation. The earlier Flask backend is archived and is not a dependency of the current browser runtime.

- Focus: Language tooling
- Stack: TypeScript, React, SVG, Python reference tooling
- [Portfolio entry](https://www.neilart.us/#dfa-visualizer)
- [Live site](https://dfa-visualizer-nr2s.vercel.app/)
- [Source code](https://github.com/NeilR2s/DFA-Visualizer)
- [Technical documentation, inspected revision](https://github.com/NeilR2s/DFA-Visualizer/blob/58ba6ea4b4bee5dc9e2e9d3ac46bf677eddc2ea5/README.md)
